stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $X = U \cup V$ with $U$ and $V$ open.
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Let $K \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$. There
is a distinguished triangle
$$
j_{U \cap V!}K|_{U \cap V} \to
j_{U!}K|_U \oplus j_{V!}K|_V \to K \to 
j_{U \cap V!}K|_{U \cap V}[1]
$$
in $D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ with obvious notation.

reason: Because restriction and lower-shriek for open embeddings are exact, it suffices to inspect the underlying short exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence j_{U∩V,!}F→j_{U,!}F⊕j_{V,!}F→F. The exactness follows on geometric stalks: elements on the overlap map anti-diagonally, and U,V cover X.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme and let
$U \subset X$ be the complement. Denote $i : Z \to X$ and $j : U \to X$
the inclusion morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Let $K \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$. There is a distinguished triangle
$$
j_!j^{-1}K \to K \to i_*i^{-1}K \to j_!j^{-1}K[1]
$$
in $D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$.

reason: The source cites the localization short exact sequence for an open complement and its closed immersion, then applies exact functors j_!, j^{-1}, i_*, i^{-1} to representatives of the derived object, giving the displayed distinguished triangle.
